rationale: Owner decision 2026-08-12 (loancalculator rebuild lane): 'keep the 12 calculator locks for the first pass and fix the planner so it looks at them and doesn't delete them.' Half 1 — matchLockedRow pairing a locked row by component identity — is LIVE (f4820a877, v1.0.1294+, council a625c326 APPROVED) but inert, because build-site-planner's load_components menu offers section/element components only: a plan structurally cannot NAME a tool component, so a rebuild re-composes each page without its tool slot and the locked calculator is exiled to the page foot with a lock_blocked_change item (the decomposition lanes' proven failure shape: seeding a site plan is the dangerous act, rerendering is not). This change widens the menu behind two gates in series so the planner can name a site's OWN, already-placed tools — and nothing else: (1) the site's current structure spec must carry plan_includes_tools='true' (fifth opt-in key on that aspect after url_shape and the three PLAN-048 identity keys; same idiom, unsafe default OFF, absent key = today's behaviour, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2); (2) the tool must already be placed on one of the planning site's own pages — content_components is GLOBAL (81 active tools), and without the placement gate a flagged site would be offered other sites' calculators. The blocker that made this more than a one-line edit is the param binding: query_database HARD-FAILS the step when a params path resolves nil ('query param path %s resolved to nil', database_actions.go:53), and load_components is the one shared planner row — a bad path is a fleet-wide planning outage. The chosen binding site_record.site_id is settled three ways: (a) the planner workflow is strictly linear (start_step read_specs -> ensure_site -> load_existing_pages -> load_components; every step exactly one next_step, no conditionals), and EnsureSiteRecordAction returns site_id on EVERY path that lets the workflow continue — the DB path (site_db_actions.go:194) and the DB-nil placeholder (:970) — with the coordinator storing that map at collected_data[output_field] (coordinator.go:1877); (b) write_site_plan in this SAME workflow has always bound the SAME path ('target_site_id': 'site_record.site_id', ExtractActionInputs Strategy 0), so every site_plans row is one live run where the path resolved — 10 rows since 2026-08-02 covering a fresh build (noted.co.uk 08-12) and repeat replans; (c) input_data.site_id was REJECTED because it is only as good as each dispatcher's input_mapping and input shapes vary by caller (extractDomainFromInput's aggressive search exists for exactly that reason; contrast 406, which used input_data.site_id for tool-suggester on the adjacent-step-already-binds-it argument — the planner has no such step and has a stronger key of its own making). QueryDatabaseAction short-circuits the initialize pass BEFORE param resolution (database_actions.go:14), so initialization cannot nil-fail. Inertness is MEASURED, not argued: old vs new query md5-identical over the full ordered row set (0ceba482d1075409bd2abd8ddebc07b8, 129 rows) for an unflagged site, for loancalculator pre-seed, and for a nonexistent site id; the post-apply STORED text re-verified 129/140/129 (unflagged/flagged/ghost) via PREPARE with an untyped parameter — the same server-side type inference the pgx stdlib driver relies on, which production exercises daily (content-quality-auditor completed runs today binding site_record.site_id against pages.site_id uuid). The flag-ON preview for loancalculator returns exactly 11 components = the 12 locked rows' distinct components (tool-loan-repayment is placed twice: index tool-3 and the archived tool-standard-calc tool-4). RFC_022 accumulation, stated rather than unremarked: this is the FIFTH opt-in key on the structure aspect. It is site_specs vocabulary, not a RegisterActionInputSpec optional key, so the 402-405 counter's N=10 action-surface budget does not count it; the structure-aspect key count now stands at 5 (url_shape, honour_realised_identity, twin_identity_snap, stem_twin_snap, plan_includes_tools). Consumers, enumerated and told (owner ruling 2026-07-29 #3): the key's readers are exactly one — this query (grep over the repo: 0 Go references; SELECT over agent_definitions: 0 rows before 407). 21 sites currently place tool components (78 placements); none is affected until its own structure spec opts in, and only loancalculator is seeded. content-gap-planner's load_available_components step carries the same section/element menu and is deliberately NOT widened — gap-planning a NEW tool page is a different authority and wants its own decision. Registered as PLAN-049 in the same commit (ordering-exemption condition 2). Config-only: live on apply, no image dependency; both DO/RAISE verify guards were induced against the pre-state and fired before the real apply.

plan.risks: The step this touches is the single shared planner menu — the failure mode that matters is a param that fails to resolve, which kills planning for EVERY site, not just flagged ones. Mitigated by binding to the same-workflow ensure_site output (present on every continuing path including the DB-nil placeholder, and the exact binding write_site_plan has exercised on every successful plan since the workflow existed) rather than to any dispatcher-shaped input; a reviewer should check that no path reaches load_components without ensure_site having completed (the workflow is linear with no conditional steps — verified against the live definition) and that the initialize pass cannot bind params (database_actions.go:14 short-circuits first). Second risk: scope creep via the global component library — the placement gate confines the widened menu to tools already on the planning site's own pages, so the planner cannot import another site's calculator; the EXISTS text comparison (->>'plan_includes_tools' = 'true') cannot error on malformed data, it just reads false. Third: fleet behaviour change for the 21 tool-placing sites if the flag spreads — each site's seeding is a deliberate per-site act (this round seeds exactly one), and the md5 control pins the unflagged result set byte-identical. Fourth: the RFC_022-shape accumulation — fifth opt-in key on the structure aspect, stated in the rationale so the seat can weigh it rather than discover it. Residual: the canary replan is the first live exercise of the widened branch; until it runs, the 140-row flagged menu is proven at the SQL layer but the planner LLM's use of the tool rows (and the identity-arm pairing end-to-end) rests on the enrichment-chain measurements of 2026-08-13.
